notes: DRAFT for scholarly review. English only; Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quranic text in the repo (Tanzil Uthmani) only; no hadith, no tafsir, no sira, no Biblical material in this phase. Hadith to add later: reports on the journey with the servant (18:60-82), on the Samiri, on the manner of the plagues and the sea, and on the death and burial of Musa. Names and details found only in later tradition are kept in unknowns_md and uncertainties_en. Quotation marks surround only speech recorded in the cited ayat (English renderings are drafts for translator and scholar review). The Quran tells Musa's account in many surahs; each chapter keeps the surahs apart and does not treat surah order as chronology. The cow of Banu Isra'il (2:67-73) is not covered in this draft. Nothing here is reviewed or published.

claims.statement_en: Allah recites to the Prophet's audience from the news of Musa and Fir'awn in truth, for a people who believe.
Fir'awn exalted himself in the land, made its people into factions, oppressed one group of them, slaughtering their sons and keeping their women alive; he was among the corrupters.

Allah says He wished to favour those who were oppressed in the land, make them leaders and inheritors, establish them in the land, and show Fir'awn, Haman and their soldiers what they feared from them.
Allah inspired the mother of Musa: “Nurse him; and when you fear for him, cast him into the river and do not fear or grieve; We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers.”

In Surah Ta-Ha, Allah reminds Musa that He had favoured him another time, when He inspired his mother what was inspired: to put him in the chest and put it into the river, so that the river would cast it up on the bank where an enemy of Allah and of Musa would take him.
Allah says He cast love from Himself upon Musa, so that he would be brought up under His eye.

chapters.summary_md: The account begins with Fir'awn's oppression of one group in his land [c2] and Allah's wish to favour the oppressed [c3]. Allah inspired the mother of Musa to nurse him and, when she feared, to cast him into the river, with a promise to return him and make him a messenger [c4]. Surah Ta-Ha tells the same favour with the chest [c5].
chapters.body_md:
Allah says He recites the news of Musa and Fir'awn in truth for a people who believe [c1]. Fir'awn exalted himself in the land and divided its people into factions, oppressing one group by slaughtering their sons and keeping their women alive [c2]. Allah says He wished to favour the oppressed, make them leaders and inheritors, and show Fir'awn, Haman and their soldiers what they feared [c3].

Allah inspired Musa's mother: nurse him, and when you fear for him, cast him into the river; do not fear or grieve; He would return him to her and make him one of the messengers [c4]. Surah Ta-Ha recalls this as a second favour: the child was to be put in a chest and the chest in the river, which would cast it on the bank, where an enemy of Allah and of Musa would take him [c5]. Allah cast love from Himself upon Musa so that he would be brought up under His eye [c6].
chapters.deep_md: Two surahs tell this decree. Surah Al-Qasas frames it with Fir'awn's policy and Allah's wish to favour the oppressed [c2][c3], then gives the instruction to the mother with a promise [c4]. Surah Ta-Ha gives the instruction as a favour recalled to Musa himself and adds the chest and the bank [c5], and the love cast upon him [c6]. The two agree on the river [c4][c5]. Haman is named already in Al-Qasas as one of the people Allah wished to show what they feared [c3].
chapters.kids_md: Fir'awn was a ruler who was unkind to a group of people in his land [c2]. Allah told the mother of Musa to nurse her baby, and when she was afraid, to put him in the river. Allah promised to give him back to her and to make him one of His messengers [c4]. Allah put love for Musa in the hearts of those who found him [c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: the passage presents a promise made before the danger was over, and a mother asked to act on it [c4]. A reader may reflect on trust when the way ahead is unclear.
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in the ayat: the name of Musa's mother, the name of the river (the ayat say yamm, 'the river' or 'the sea'), the date, the number of years of the oppression, and the name or dynasty of Fir'awn. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the personal names of Musa's mother and sister, the name of the river, and any dates. The sentence at 28:6 says Haman; the Quran gives no further detail on his office. Hadith to add later: none identified for this chapter.

claims.statement_en: The family of Fir'awn picked him up so that he would become to them an enemy and a grief; Allah says Fir'awn, Haman and their soldiers were sinners.
The wife of Fir'awn said “A joy of the eye for me and for you; do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son”, and they did not perceive.
The heart of Musa's mother became empty; she was about to disclose it had Allah not strengthened her heart so that she would be among the believers.
She told his sister to follow him; the sister watched him from a distance while they did not perceive.
Allah had forbidden wet-nurses to him beforehand; the sister said “Shall I direct you to a household who will take care of him for you and be sincere to him?”
Allah returned him to his mother so that her eye would be cooled and she would not grieve, and so that she would know that Allah's promise is true.
Later, Fir'awn said to Musa “Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you stayed among us for years of your life?”

chapters.summary_md: The family of Fir'awn picked him up [c1], and Fir'awn's wife said not to kill him [c2]. His mother's heart was emptied and Allah strengthened it [c3]. His sister followed him [c4], asked whether she could direct them to a household to nurse him [c5], and Allah returned him to his mother [c6]. Fir'awn later reminded Musa that he had been raised among them [c7].
chapters.body_md: The family of Fir'awn picked up the child so that he would become to them an enemy and a grief [c1]. The wife of Fir'awn said he was a joy of the eye for her and for Fir'awn, that they should not kill him, and that perhaps he would benefit them or be adopted as a son; they did not perceive [c2]. The heart of Musa's mother became empty, and she would nearly have disclosed him had Allah not strengthened her heart [c3]. She told his sister to follow him, and the sister watched from a distance while they did not perceive [c4]. Allah had forbidden wet-nurses to the child beforehand, and the sister said she could direct them to a household who would take care of him and be sincere to him [c5]. Allah returned him to his mother so that her eye would be cooled, she would not grieve, and she would know that Allah's promise is true [c6]. Surah Ash-Shu'ara records Fir'awn later reminding Musa that he had been raised among them as a child and had stayed for years of his life [c7].
chapters.deep_md: Surah Al-Qasas and Surah Ta-Ha both end the return with the mother's eye cooled and no more grief [c6]. Only Al-Qasas shows the sister's words and the wife's [c2][c5]. The sentence in which Allah says the family picked him up “so that he would become to them an enemy” [c1] sits next to the sentence where Fir'awn's wife says “a joy of the eye” [c2]; the text records both without reconciling them in words.
chapters.kids_md: Fir'awn's family found the baby. Fir'awn's wife said, “Do not kill him; perhaps he will help us” [c2]. Musa's sister watched from far away and asked whether she could find someone to care for him [c4][c5]. So Allah gave Musa back to his mother, and she was happy [c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: the account shows the mother's fear and Allah's strengthening of her heart [c3], and a promise kept [c6]. It also records a good word from an unexpected person in the palace of an unjust ruler [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in the ayat: the names of the wife of Fir'awn (Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text), of Musa's sister, and of the nursing household; the length of time; where in Fir'awn's household he lived (the ayat do not describe a building; this draft does not say palace). Whether the “years” in 26:18 refers to this period or a longer one is not stated.

claims.statement_en: When he reached his full strength and was established, Allah gave him judgement and knowledge.

He entered the city at a time of heedlessness of its people and found two men fighting, one from his party and one from his enemy; the one from his party asked him for help against the one from his enemy; Musa struck him and ended his life.
Musa said “This is of the work of Shaytan; he is a manifest misleading enemy.”
He said “My Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me”, and Allah forgave him; and he said “My Lord, for the favour You have shown me, I will never be a supporter of the criminals.”
In the morning he was in the city fearful and watching; the one who had asked for his help the day before cried out to him again, and Musa said to him “You are clearly a deviant.”

When he wished to seize the one who was an enemy to both of them, a speaker said “Musa, do you want to kill me as you killed a person yesterday? You only want to be a tyrant in the land and do not want to be among the reformers.”
A man came running from the far end of the city and said “Musa, the chiefs are conspiring about you to kill you, so leave; I am to you one of the sincere advisers.”
He left fearful and watching, saying “My Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people.”

Fir'awn later said “You did your deed which you did, and you were of the ungrateful”; Musa replied “I did it then while I was among those who erred; I fled from you when I feared you; then my Lord gave me judgement and made me one of the messengers.”
Allah reminds Musa that he killed a person and Allah delivered him from distress and tried him with trials.

chapters.summary_md: Musa was given judgement and knowledge [c1]. In the city he struck a man who died [c2], called it the work of Shaytan, and asked forgiveness [c3][c4]. Next morning he was warned that the chiefs were conspiring to kill him [c7], and he left, asking to be saved from the wrongdoing people [c8].
chapters.body_md:
When Musa reached his full strength, Allah gave him judgement and knowledge [c1]. He entered the city when its people were heedless and found two men fighting; the one from his party asked for his help against his enemy, Musa struck the other, and ended his life [c2]. He said it was of the work of Shaytan, a manifest misleading enemy [c3], and asked his Lord to forgive him, which Allah did; he said he would never be a supporter of the criminals [c4].

In the morning he was fearful and watching; the man who had asked for his help the day before cried out again, and Musa called him a clear deviant [c5]. As Musa wished to seize the one who was an enemy to both, a speaker said he wanted to be a tyrant and not a reformer, asking if he meant to kill as he had killed the day before [c6]. A man came running from the far end of the city with a warning that the chiefs were conspiring to kill him, and told him to leave [c7]. Musa left, fearful and watching, and asked to be saved from the wrongdoing people [c8].

Later accounts recall the event. Fir'awn says Musa did his deed and was of the ungrateful, and Musa answers that he did it when he erred, fled from fear, and that his Lord then gave him judgement and made him a messenger [c9]. Surah Ta-Ha recalls that Allah delivered him from distress and tried him with trials [c10].
chapters.deep_md: The three surahs agree on the killing and the fear [c2][c9][c10]. Only Al-Qasas gives the sequence of the two days [c2][c5], the prayer for forgiveness and the forgiveness [c4], and the running man [c7]. In Ash-Shu'ara, Musa's own account is brief and ties the flight to fear [c9]. The speaker of 28:19 is not named in the text, and the ayah does not say whether it is the man whom Musa had helped or the other man. The ayat call the first act the work of Shaytan [c3] and Musa calls himself one who “wronged himself” [c4].
chapters.kids_md: One day in the city Musa tried to help a man, and a fight ended in a man's death. Musa was sorry and asked Allah to forgive him, and Allah forgave him [c2][c4]. A man ran to warn him that the chiefs wanted to harm him, and Musa left the city and asked Allah to save him [c7][c8].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: the account records a prophet admitting a wrong, asking for forgiveness, and being forgiven [c4]. A reader may reflect on how a person responds after a mistake.
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in the ayat: which of the two men is meant by “from his party” and “from his enemy” beyond those words, the name of the city, who spoke in 28:19 (interpreters differ), how Musa struck the man, the name of the man who warned him (Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text), and the length of the interval between the events. Ash-Shu'ara 26:20 uses a word that interpreters render in different ways (“erred”, “was unaware”); this draft gives one rendering for review.

claims.statement_en: As he turned toward Madyan he said “Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way.”

At the water of Madyan he found a group of people watering and, apart from them, two women holding back; he asked “What is your affair?” and they said “We cannot water until the shepherds leave, and our father is an old man.”
He watered for them, withdrew to the shade, and said “My Lord, I am in need of whatever good You send down to me.”

One of the two came to him walking shyly and said “My father invites you to pay you the reward for watering for us”; when he came to the father and told him his story, the father said “Do not fear; you have escaped from the wrongdoing people.”
One of the two said “Father, hire him; the best you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy.”

The father said he wished to marry one of his two daughters to him on condition that he serve him for eight years, and that if he completed ten it would be from him; he did not wish to burden him, and Musa would find him, if Allah willed, among the righteous.
Musa said “That is between me and you; whichever of the two terms I complete, there is no injustice to me; and Allah is a witness over what we say.”
Surah Ta-Ha says he stayed for years among the people of Madyan and then came at a decreed time.

chapters.summary_md: Musa turned toward Madyan [c1], helped two women at the water [c2][c3], was invited by their father [c4], and was offered a marriage in return for service for eight years, with ten as a favour [c6]. He accepted the terms [c7]. Surah Ta-Ha says he stayed years among the people of Madyan [c8].
chapters.body_md:
As Musa turned toward Madyan he said he hoped his Lord would guide him to the right way [c1]. At the water he found people watering and two women holding back; they told him they could not water until the shepherds left and that their father was an old man [c2]. He watered for them, withdrew to the shade, and said he was in need of whatever good Allah would send to him [c3]. One of them came shyly to invite him from her father to be paid for the watering; the father, hearing his story, told him not to fear for he had escaped the wrongdoing people [c4]. One said her father should hire him as the strong and trustworthy [c5].

The father offered to marry him to one of his two daughters in return for eight years of service, with ten as a favour from Musa if he completed them [c6]. Musa agreed to the terms and made Allah a witness [c7]. Surah Ta-Ha says Musa stayed for years among the people of Madyan and then came at a decreed time [c8].
chapters.deep_md: The passage is one of the few in Musa's account with the details of an ordinary agreement: the work, the term and the marriage [c6][c7]. The terms are given as a choice of two lengths, with the longer a favour [c6]; Musa's reply refers to “the two terms” [c7]. The text says nothing of what Musa did with the flock beyond the words ‘hire’ and ‘serve’. The prayer in the shade [c3] is the only speech of Musa to Allah recorded between the flight and the fire in Al-Qasas.
chapters.kids_md: Musa came to the water of Madyan and saw two women who could not get water for their sheep. He helped them [c2][c3]. Their father invited him, and later offered him work and a marriage. Musa agreed [c6][c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: Musa helps without being asked and then asks Allah for good [c3]. The father's offer is made with a plain statement of terms [c6], and the daughter's description of a good worker is “strong and trustworthy” [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in the ayat: the name of the father and of his daughters; whether the father was a prophet (Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: a name linking him to Shu'ayb, whom the Quran elsewhere sends to Madyan, but the ayat here do not make that link); the location of Madyan; which of the two terms Musa completed (the ayat say only that he completed the term, 28:29); and the name of the daughter he married.

claims.statement_en: When Musa had completed the term and set out with his family, he perceived a fire on the side of the mountain (at-Tur) and said to his family “Stay here; I have perceived a fire; perhaps I will bring you news from it, or a burning brand from the fire so that you may warm yourselves.”
When he came to it he was called from the right side of the valley, in the blessed spot, from the tree: “Musa, I am Allah, the Lord of the worlds.”
In Surah Ta-Ha he was called “Musa, I am your Lord, so take off your sandals; you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.”
He was told “I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed; I am Allah, there is no god but Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.”

He was told that the Hour is coming, which Allah almost keeps hidden, so that every soul is recompensed for its striving, and not to let the one who does not believe in it and follows his desire turn him from it.
In Surah An-Naml the call says “Blessed is whoever is in the fire and whoever is around it, and glory be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. Musa, it is I, Allah, the Almighty, the Wise.”
In Surah An-Nazi'at, Allah asks if the account of Musa has reached the listener, when his Lord called him in the sacred valley of Tuwa.
In Surah Maryam, Musa is described as one chosen (mukhlas), a messenger and a prophet; Allah called him from the right side of the mountain and brought him near in private converse.

chapters.summary_md: On the way with his family Musa saw a fire and went to bring news or a brand from it [c1]. He was called from the valley, “I am Allah, the Lord of the worlds” [c2], told to take off his sandals [c3], told that he was chosen, to worship Allah and establish prayer [c4], and told of the coming Hour [c5].
chapters.body_md: Musa, having completed the term and set out with his family, perceived a fire on the side of the mountain and told his family to stay while he went to bring news from it or a burning brand [c1]. As he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley, in the blessed spot, from the tree: “Musa, I am Allah, the Lord of the worlds” [c2]. In Surah Ta-Ha the call also says “I am your Lord, so take off your sandals; you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa” [c3], that he has been chosen and should listen to what is revealed, that Allah is Allah, there is no god but Him, to worship Him and establish prayer for His remembrance [c4], and that the Hour is coming [c5]. Surah An-Naml adds the call “Blessed is whoever is in the fire and whoever is around it” and “Musa, it is I, Allah, the Almighty, the Wise” [c6]. Surah An-Nazi'at recalls the call in the sacred valley of Tuwa [c7]. Surah Maryam describes Musa as chosen, a messenger and a prophet, called from the right side of the mountain and brought near in private converse [c8].
chapters.deep_md: Five surahs refer to this moment. They agree on the fire [c1], the valley [c3][c7], the right side of the mountain [c2][c8], and the call by name [c2][c3][c6]. The call is described in Al-Qasas as coming “from the tree” [c2]; the ayat do not say more about the tree. Different surahs give different parts of what Musa was told: the identity of the caller [c2][c6], the command to take off his sandals [c3], the central message of worship and prayer [c4], and the coming Hour [c5]. These are complementary parts of one scene in the text; the ayat do not say that these are separate occasions.
chapters.kids_md: Musa saw a fire from far away and went toward it to bring his family some news or a piece of it to warm them [c1]. A voice called out: “Musa, I am Allah, the Lord of the worlds” [c2]. Allah told him to take off his sandals because he was in a holy valley [c3]. Allah told him to worship Him and to pray [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: Musa went toward a fire to help his family and was met with a call. The message he received first is about worship and prayer [c4], and the reminder that every soul will be recompensed [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in the ayat: the exact place or the date, what the fire was, what the tree was, which night, and the names of those with him. The ayat say 'his family'; they do not list them. The caller's voice is described only as a call. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name of the place on the mountain. Whether “whoever is in the fire” (27:8) names a specific being is read differently by interpreters; this draft makes no claim.

chapters.title_en: The staff, the hand and Harun

claims.statement_en: Allah asked “What is that in your right hand, Musa?” and he said “It is my staff; I lean on it, I beat down leaves with it for my sheep, and I have other uses for it.”
He was told to throw it, and it became a moving snake; he was told “Take it and do not fear; We will return it to its first state.”

In Surah Al-Qasas and Surah An-Naml, when he saw it moving as if it were a snake, he turned in flight and did not look back; he was told to come forward and not to fear, that he was secure, and that the messengers do not fear in Allah's presence.

He was told to draw his hand to his side or put it in his bosom, and it would come out white without harm, as another sign; these are two proofs from his Lord to Fir'awn and his chiefs, who were a defiantly disobedient people, among nine signs.
He was told to go to Fir'awn, who had transgressed.

Musa prayed “My Lord, expand my chest for me, ease my task for me, and loosen the knot from my tongue so that they understand my speech; appoint for me a minister from my family, Harun my brother; strengthen my back with him and let him share in my task, so that we may glorify You much and remember You much; You are ever seeing us.” Allah said “You have been given your request, Musa.”

In Surah Al-Qasas, he said “My Lord, I killed a person among them, so I fear they will kill me; my brother Harun is more fluent than I in speech, so send him with me as support to confirm me; I fear they will deny me.”
Allah said “We will strengthen your arm with your brother and give you both authority so that they cannot reach you; with Our signs, you two and those who follow you will be the victors.”
In Surah Maryam, Allah says He granted Musa, out of His mercy, his brother Harun as a prophet.

chapters.summary_md: Musa was asked about what was in his hand and answered it was his staff [c1]. It became a moving snake and then was returned to its first state [c2]; he was told not to fear [c3]. His hand came out white as a second sign [c4]. He was sent to Fir'awn [c5] and prayed for ease, and for Harun to be with him [c6][c7]. Allah granted the request [c6][c8][c9].
chapters.body_md:
Allah asked Musa what was in his right hand, and he said it was his staff, on which he leaned and with which he beat down leaves for his sheep, with other uses besides [c1]. He was told to throw it, and it became a moving snake; he was told to take it without fear, for it would return to its first state [c2]. In Al-Qasas and An-Naml he turned in flight and was told to come forward, that he was secure, and that messengers do not fear in Allah's presence [c3]. He was told to put his hand into his bosom, and it would come out white without harm, as another sign, among nine signs to Fir'awn and his people, who were defiantly disobedient [c4]. He was told to go to Fir'awn, who had transgressed [c5].

In Surah Ta-Ha, Musa then prayed for his chest to be expanded, his task eased, the knot loosened from his tongue so that they would understand his speech, and for Harun his brother as a minister to strengthen his back and share in his task; Allah answered that his request was granted [c6]. In Al-Qasas he gave the reason: he had killed a person among them and feared being killed, and Harun was more fluent in speech [c7]. Allah said He would strengthen his arm with his brother and give both authority, so that they could not be reached, and they and their followers would be the victors [c8]. Surah Maryam says Allah granted Musa, from His mercy, his brother Harun as a prophet [c9].
chapters.deep_md: The signs of the staff and the hand are told in three surahs with different emphasis. Ta-Ha has the question about the staff and the gentle command to take the snake [c1][c2]. Al-Qasas and An-Naml have Musa's flight and the reassurance [c3]. The request for Harun is given in two forms: the prayer for ease and a helper in Ta-Ha [c6] and the reasons of the killing and fluency in Al-Qasas [c7]. Allah's answer in Al-Qasas speaks of authority and victory [c8] and Maryam names Harun as a prophet [c9]. An-Naml and Al-Qasas call the signs “nine signs” and “two proofs” respectively [c4]; the ayat in this draft do not list the nine.
chapters.kids_md: Allah asked Musa what he held, and he said it was his staff. Allah told him to throw it, and it became a moving snake. Then Allah told him not to be afraid [c1][c2][c3]. Allah gave him another sign with his hand [c4]. Musa asked Allah to make his task easy and to send his brother Harun to help him, and Allah said yes [c6][c9].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: Musa does not simply accept the task; he asks for ease, for clearer speech, and for his brother's help [c6]. The record shows asking for help before a hard task.
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in these ayat: what the nine signs are (the plagues are listed elsewhere, in 7:133, in the chapter on the years of pressure, and they are not assumed to be the nine); what was the nature of the “knot” in Musa's tongue (the ayat state only the request); the age of Harun relative to Musa; where Harun was when he was sent for. Hadith to add later: reports on the staff and on the knot in the tongue.

claims.statement_en: Allah told Musa and his brother to go with His signs and not slacken in remembering Him, to go to Fir'awn who had transgressed, and to speak to him a gentle word, so that perhaps he would remember or fear.
They said “Our Lord, we fear that he will hasten against us or transgress”; Allah said “Do not fear; I am with you both, hearing and seeing.”

In Surah Ash-Shu'ara, Allah called Musa to go to the wrongdoing people, the people of Fir'awn, asking “Will they not be mindful?”; Musa said “My Lord, I fear that they will deny me, my chest is straitened and my tongue is not fluent, so send for Harun; they also have a charge against me, so I fear they will kill me”; Allah said “No; go both of you with Our signs; We are with you, listening.”

They were to say to Fir'awn “We are two messengers of your Lord (the messenger of the Lord of the worlds): send the Children of Israel with us and do not torment them; we have come to you with a sign from your Lord; peace be upon the one who follows the guidance.”

Fir'awn said “Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you stayed among us for years of your life? And you did your deed which you did, and you were of the ungrateful.” Musa said that he had done it then while he erred, fled when he feared, and was then given judgement and made one of the messengers.
Musa said “That is a favour you hold over me: that you have enslaved the Children of Israel.” (Interpreters read this sentence as a statement or as a question.)

Fir'awn asked “Who is your Lord, Musa?” and Musa said “Our Lord is He who gave everything its form and then guided.” Fir'awn asked about the earlier generations and Musa said their knowledge is with his Lord in a record; his Lord neither errs nor forgets.

In Surah Ash-Shu'ara, Fir'awn asked “And what is the Lord of the worlds?” Musa answered “The Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, if you are convinced”, then “Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers”, then “The Lord of the east and the west and what is between them, if you use reason.”
Fir'awn said to those around him “Do you not hear?” and said “Your messenger who was sent to you is surely mad.”
Fir'awn said “If you take a god other than me, I will make you one of the imprisoned.” Musa said “Even if I bring you something clear?” Fir'awn said “Bring it, if you are of the truthful.”
In Surah An-Nazi'at, Musa was told to go to Fir'awn, who had transgressed, and to say “Would you be purified, and shall I guide you to your Lord so that you fear?”

chapters.summary_md: Musa and Harun were sent to Fir'awn with a gentle word [c1], having voiced their fear and been told Allah was with them [c2][c3]. Their message was to send the Children of Israel with them [c4]. Fir'awn reminded Musa of the years in his household [c5], asked who the Lord is [c7][c8], called Musa mad [c9] and threatened prison [c10].
chapters.body_md:
Allah told Musa and his brother to go to Fir'awn with His signs, not to slacken in remembering Him, and to speak a gentle word so that perhaps Fir'awn would remember or fear [c1]. They said they feared he would hasten against them or transgress, and Allah said He was with them, hearing and seeing [c2]. In Ash-Shu'ara Musa voiced fear of being denied, his tongue not being fluent, and a charge against him, and asked that Harun be sent for; Allah said to go with His signs and that He was listening [c3].

The message was that they were messengers and that Fir'awn should send the Children of Israel with them and not torment them, with peace on the one who follows the guidance [c4]. Fir'awn answered by recalling the years Musa stayed with them and his deed, and Musa replied that he had done it while he erred, fled from fear, and was given judgement and made a messenger [c5]. Musa said the favour Fir'awn held over him was that he had enslaved the Children of Israel [c6].

Fir'awn asked who the Lord is; in Ta-Ha Musa answered that He gave everything its form and then guided, and that the knowledge of earlier generations is with his Lord in a record [c7]. In Ash-Shu'ara he answered with the Lord of the heavens and the earth, of the forefathers, and of the east and the west [c8]. Fir'awn asked those around if they heard and called Musa mad [c9], then threatened to imprison him if he took a god other than Fir'awn; Musa asked if he would do so even if he brought something clear [c10]. Surah An-Nazi'at records the message in the form of a question about purification and guidance [c11].
chapters.deep_md: The meeting is told in three surahs that each preserve a different part of the exchange. Ta-Ha contains the instruction to speak gently and Allah's assurance [c1][c2]. Ash-Shu'ara contains Musa's fears [c3], Fir'awn's reminder of his upbringing and deed [c5][c6], and the series of questions [c8]. An-Nazi'at has the message in the form of a question [c11]. Fir'awn's two statements about Musa, “mad” [c9] and “imprisoned” [c10], are in Ash-Shu'ara only. The text records Musa's answers as statements about the Lord and does not report Fir'awn's reply to each.
chapters.kids_md: Allah told Musa and Harun to speak to Fir'awn kindly. They were a little afraid, and Allah told them He was with them, hearing and seeing [c1][c2]. They asked Fir'awn to let the Children of Israel go with them [c4]. Fir'awn asked who their Lord was, and Musa said He is the one who gave everything its shape and then guided it [c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: the instruction to a messenger facing a tyrant is to speak a gentle word first [c1], and the assurance given to the frightened is that Allah is hearing and seeing [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in the ayat: where the meeting took place, how many times it happened, which of the surahs describes the first meeting, and the personal name or period of this Fir'awn (Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: any identification with a named ruler of Egypt; none is used here). The word in 20:50 translated “gave everything its form” and the sentence in 79:18 have more than one possible rendering for scholarly review.

claims.statement_en: Allah sent Musa with His signs to Fir'awn and his chiefs; Musa said “Fir'awn, I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds, bound to say nothing about Allah but the truth; I have come to you with clear proof from your Lord, so send the Children of Israel with me.”
Fir'awn said “If you have come with a sign, bring it, if you are of the truthful.” Musa threw his staff and it was a clear serpent; he drew out his hand and it was white to the onlookers.

The chiefs said “This is a learned magician who wants to drive you out of your land”, and Fir'awn asked what they advise; they said to delay him and his brother and send gatherers into the cities to bring every learned magician.

Allah sent Musa and Harun to Fir'awn and his chiefs; they were arrogant and a criminal people; when the truth came, they said “This is clear magic”, and Musa said “Do you say this of the truth when it has come to you? Is this magic? The magicians do not succeed.”
They said “Have you come to turn us from what we found our fathers following, so that greatness in the land may be yours? We are not believers in you two.”
They said “Shall we believe two humans like ourselves, whose people are servants to us?”, denied them, and were among the destroyed.

They said “This is nothing but forged magic, and we never heard of this among our earlier forefathers”; Musa said “My Lord knows best who comes with guidance from Him and who will have the final home; the wrongdoers do not succeed.”

Fir'awn said “Chiefs, I do not know of any god for you other than me; so kindle for me, Haman, a fire upon clay and build me a tower so that I may look at the God of Musa; I think he is one of the liars.”

In Surah Ghafir, Musa was sent with signs and clear authority to Fir'awn, Haman and Qarun, who said “a magician, a liar”; when he brought the truth they said to kill the sons of those who believed with him and keep their women alive.

Fir'awn said “Let me kill Musa and let him call upon his Lord; I fear that he will change your religion or cause corruption to appear in the land.” Musa said “I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Account.”

A believing man from the family of Fir'awn, who was concealing his faith, asked “Would you kill a man because he says ‘My Lord is Allah’, when he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord? If he is a liar, his lie is upon him; if he is truthful, some of what he promises will strike you.”

In Surah An-Nazi'at, Musa showed him the greatest sign, and he denied and disobeyed, turned away striving, gathered, and called out “I am your lord, the most high”; Allah seized him with the punishment of the last and the first; in that is a lesson for whoever fears.

chapters.summary_md: Musa brought clear proof and asked Fir'awn to send the Children of Israel with him [c1]. He showed the staff and the hand [c2]. The chiefs called it magic and proposed gathering magicians [c3][c4]. Fir'awn claimed a position no other god was known to the chiefs [c8] and spoke of killing Musa [c10]; a believer from his family spoke against it [c11].
chapters.body_md:
Musa told Fir'awn that he was a messenger from the Lord of the worlds, bound to say only the truth, with clear proof, and asked him to send the Children of Israel with him [c1]. Fir'awn said to bring a sign if he was truthful; Musa threw his staff and it was a clear serpent, and his hand came out white to the onlookers [c2]. The chiefs said he was a learned magician who wanted to drive them out of the land, and advised gathering every learned magician [c3].

Surah Yunus says that when the truth came they called it clear magic, and Musa asked how they could call it magic when magicians do not succeed [c4]; they replied that he came to turn them from their fathers' way and to gain greatness in the land [c5]. Surah Al-Mu'minun records them saying they would not believe two humans like themselves whose people served them [c6]. Surah Al-Qasas records the answer ‘forged magic’ and Musa's reply that his Lord knows best who brings guidance [c7], and Fir'awn's saying that he knew no god for the chiefs but himself and his order to Haman to build a tower [c8]. Surah Ghafir names Fir'awn, Haman and Qarun, who said ‘a magician, a liar’, and ordered the killing of the sons of the believers [c9]. Fir'awn said he wished to kill Musa, fearing for their religion; Musa sought refuge in his Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Account [c10]. A believing man from Fir'awn's family concealing his faith asked whether they would kill a man for saying ‘My Lord is Allah’ [c11]. Surah An-Nazi'at tells that Fir'awn denied and disobeyed, gathered, and said “I am your lord, the most high”, and was seized [c12].
chapters.deep_md: Passages from seven surahs share one pattern: a sign is shown and called magic [c2][c4][c7][c9], those in authority respond with fear of loss of land and ancestral ways [c3][c5][c10], and Fir'awn makes a claim for himself [c8][c12]. In Surah Ghafir the account adds a figure not seen elsewhere in this draft, a believing man in Fir'awn's own family [c11]. The ayat do not say how long this period lasted or in what order these exchanges took place. The wording of the “punishment of the last and the first” in An-Nazi'at [c12] has more than one reading among interpreters and is left for a scholar.
chapters.kids_md: Musa showed Fir'awn the signs Allah gave him [c2]. Fir'awn and his chiefs said it was magic [c4][c7]. Fir'awn said he knew of no god for them but himself [c8]. One man in Fir'awn's family secretly believed, and he asked, “Would you kill a man because he says ‘My Lord is Allah’?” [c11].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: the account notes that clear signs can be explained away by those who fear to lose position [c3][c5], and that a single voice from inside such a court spoke in defence of what was right [c11].
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in the ayat: the time and place of each appearance before the court; the number of conversations; the identity and name of the believing man (Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text; none is used here); who Qarun and Haman were beyond what is said in the ayat (their own accounts are in separate records); and the content of the “greatest sign” in 79:20 (interpreters differ on whether it is the staff, the hand or both).

claims.statement_en: In Surah Ta-Ha, Fir'awn said “Have you come to drive us out of our land with your magic, Musa? We will bring you magic like it; so set an appointment between us and you, which neither we nor you shall fail, at a place midway.” Musa said “Your appointment is the day of the festival, and let the people be gathered at forenoon.”
Fir'awn turned away, gathered his plan, then came; Musa said to them “Woe to you, do not invent a lie against Allah, lest He destroy you with a punishment; whoever invents has failed.”
The magicians were gathered for the appointed time of a known day, and the people were asked whether they would gather, so that they might follow the magicians if they were the victors.
The magicians asked Fir'awn whether they would have a reward if they were the victors; he said “Yes, and you will then be among those brought near.”
They said “Musa, either you throw, or we will be the ones to throw”; he said “Throw.” When they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people and terrified them and brought great magic.

Their ropes and staffs seemed to Musa, from their magic, to be moving, and Musa felt fear within himself; Allah said “Do not fear; you are the uppermost. Throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow what they have made; what they have made is only the trick of a magician, and the magician does not succeed wherever he comes.”
Musa threw his staff and it swallowed what they fabricated; the truth was established and what they were doing was made void, and they were defeated there and turned back humbled.

In Surah Yunus, Musa said to the magicians “Throw what you will throw”, and after they threw, “What you have brought is magic; Allah will make it vain; Allah does not set right the work of the corrupters; and Allah establishes the truth by His words, even if the criminals dislike it.”
The magicians were cast down in prostration, saying “We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun” (Ta-Ha has “the Lord of Harun and Musa”).

Fir'awn said “You believed him before I gave you permission? He is your chief who taught you magic. I will cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides and I will crucify you all.” (Ta-Ha says on the trunks of palm trees.)

They said “No harm; to our Lord we will return; we hope that our Lord will forgive us our faults because we were the first of the believers”, and “You take revenge on us only because we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us. Our Lord, pour patience upon us and take us in death as Muslims.”

In Surah Ta-Ha, they said “We will never prefer you over the clear proofs that came to us and over Him who created us; so decree whatever you decree; you only decree for this worldly life. We have believed in our Lord so that He may forgive us our faults and the magic to which you compelled us; Allah is better and more lasting.”

chapters.summary_md: A day was set for Musa and the magicians [c1][c3]. The magicians threw first [c5] and it seemed to Musa that their ropes moved [c6]. His staff swallowed what they had made [c7]. The magicians fell down in prostration and said they believed in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun [c9]. Fir'awn threatened them [c10], and they answered with patience and hope for forgiveness [c11][c12].
chapters.body_md:
Fir'awn proposed an appointment between his magicians and Musa, and Musa set the day of the festival, with the people gathered at forenoon [c1]. Fir'awn gathered his plan and came; Musa warned them not to invent a lie against Allah [c2]. The people were asked to gather in case the magicians won [c3], and the magicians asked for a reward, which Fir'awn promised, with nearness to him [c4]. They asked whether Musa would throw first; he told them to throw, and they bewitched the eyes of the people and brought great magic [c5]. Their ropes and staffs seemed to move and Musa felt fear within himself; Allah told him not to fear, that he was uppermost, and to throw what was in his right hand [c6]. His staff swallowed what they had fabricated, the truth was established and they were defeated [c7]. Surah Yunus gives Musa's words after they threw: that Allah will make it vain and establishes the truth by His words [c8].

The magicians were cast down in prostration, saying “We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun” [c9]. Fir'awn said they had believed before his permission, that Musa was their chief who taught them magic, and that he would cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides and crucify them [c10]. They answered that there was no harm, that they would return to their Lord and hoped for forgiveness [c11], and in Ta-Ha that they would not prefer him over the clear proofs and over Him who created them [c12].
chapters.deep_md: The day of the magicians is told in four surahs, with parallel structure and different speakers in each. Surah Ta-Ha gives the scene-setting by Fir'awn and Musa [c1][c2] and Musa's fear [c6]. Ash-Shu'ara and Al-A'raf have the reward and the dialogue of the magicians [c4][c5] and the swallowing [c7]. The words of the magicians after their prostration are given in three forms: in Ash-Shu'ara and Al-A'raf with ‘Lord of the worlds’ [c9], with fuller responses in each [c11], and in Ta-Ha with the declaration against the threat [c12]. The ayat of Ta-Ha after 73 speak of the end of the criminal and the believer; they are not claimed here because their speaker is not marked.
chapters.kids_md: Fir'awn gathered his magicians to show that Musa was not truthful. They threw their ropes and sticks, and it seemed to Musa that they were moving. Allah told him not to fear and to throw his staff [c5][c6]. His staff swallowed what the magicians had made, and the magicians fell down and said, “We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun” [c7][c9].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: the magicians were the experts of their craft, and they recognised what they saw as different from their own work [c7][c9]. They then held to their belief when threatened [c11][c12].
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in the ayat: how many magicians there were, the place and date of the festival (the ayat say “the day of the festival” and “forenoon”), the nature of their ropes and staffs beyond that they seemed to move, and whether the sentence in 7:116 and 20:66 describe two different moments. The ayat on the magicians' fate after the threat are not narrated; this draft makes no claim about it.

claims.statement_en: The chiefs asked Fir'awn “Will you leave Musa and his people to spread corruption in the land and leave you and your gods?” He said “We will kill their sons and keep their women alive, and we are dominant over them.”
Musa said to his people “Seek help in Allah and be patient; the earth is Allah's; He gives it as an inheritance to whom He wills of His servants; and the end is for the mindful.”
They said “We were harmed before you came to us and after you came to us.” He said “Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land, and then see how you act.”

Allah seized the people of Fir'awn with years of drought and a shortage of fruits, so that they might remember; when good came they said it was theirs, and when evil struck they blamed Musa and those with him as an omen; Allah says their omen is with Him.
They said “Whatever sign you bring to bewitch us with, we will not believe you.”
Allah sent upon them the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood as detailed signs; they were arrogant and a criminal people.

When the plague fell on them they said “Musa, call upon your Lord for us by what He has covenanted with you; if you remove the plague from us, we will believe you and send the Children of Israel with you”; when Allah removed it for a term which they were to reach, they broke their word.
None believed Musa except some of the offspring (dhurriyyah) of his people, in fear that Fir'awn and his chiefs would persecute them; Fir'awn was high in the land and among the transgressors.

Musa said “My people, if you have believed in Allah, then rely upon Him, if you are Muslims”; they said “In Allah we put our trust. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people, and save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people.”

Allah inspired Musa and his brother to settle their people in houses in Misr, to make their houses a qiblah (the Arabic word qiblah is left untranslated here), to establish prayer, and to give good news to the believers.

Musa said “Our Lord, You gave Fir'awn and his chiefs adornment and wealth in the life of this world; our Lord, that they may lead astray from Your way; our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts, so that they do not believe until they see the painful punishment.” Allah said “Your supplication has been answered, so be upright and do not follow the way of those who do not know.”

chapters.summary_md: Fir'awn's chiefs urged him against Musa and his people, and he said he would kill their sons [c1]. Musa told his people to seek Allah's help and be patient [c2]. Drought, shortage [c4] and five named signs [c6] came on Fir'awn's people. They promised to believe if relieved and broke their word [c7]. Only some of the offspring of his people believed, in fear [c8]; Musa and his brother were told to settle their people in houses and establish prayer [c10].
chapters.body_md:
The chiefs asked Fir'awn if he would leave Musa and his people to spread corruption and abandon him and his gods, and he said he would kill their sons and keep their women alive [c1]. Musa told his people to seek help in Allah and be patient, because the earth is Allah's and He gives it to whom He wills [c2]. They said they had been harmed before and after he came; he said that perhaps their Lord would destroy their enemy and make them successors, and see how they would act [c3].

Allah seized Fir'awn's people with years of drought and shortage of fruit so that they would remember; they credited good to themselves and blamed Musa and those with him for evil, and Allah says their omen is with Him [c4]. They said no sign would make them believe [c5]. Allah sent the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood as detailed signs, and they were arrogant [c6]. When the plague fell they asked Musa to call upon his Lord, promising to believe and to send the Children of Israel; when it was removed they broke their word [c7].

Surah Yunus says none believed Musa except some of the offspring (dhurriyyah) of his people, for fear of Fir'awn [c8]. Musa told them to rely upon Allah, and they said they trusted in Allah and asked not to be a trial for the wrongdoers and to be saved [c9]. Allah inspired Musa and his brother to settle their people in houses in Misr, to establish prayer and to give good news to the believers [c10]. Musa prayed about Fir'awn's adornment and wealth, and Allah said his supplication had been answered and told them to be upright [c11].
chapters.deep_md: The two passages give different sides of the same period. Al-A'raf records the pressure and the signs [c1][c4][c6][c7]; Yunus records the limited number of believers and their prayers [c8][c9][c11]. The five signs of 7:133 [c6] are not claimed to be the nine signs mentioned in other surahs, and the ayat do not match the two lists. The Arabic word dhurriyyah in [c8] (offspring, descendants) is understood in more than one way by interpreters.
chapters.kids_md: Fir'awn was unkind to Musa's people. Musa told them to ask Allah for help and to be patient [c2]. Allah sent signs to Fir'awn's people so that they would remember [c4][c6]. They promised to believe if the trouble stopped, but when it stopped they did not keep their word [c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: the account shows a promise made in hardship and broken in ease [c7]. It also shows a small group asking Allah for protection and trust in Him [c9].
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in the ayat: the order, length and number of the plagues beyond the five named in 7:133; how many believed; who the dhurriyyah were (the ayat say ‘offspring of his people’); and the meaning of making houses a qiblah in 10:87 (interpreters differ: facing, place of prayer). Hadith to add later: reports on the plagues.

claims.statement_en: Allah inspired Musa “Travel by night with My servants; you will be pursued.”
Fir'awn sent gatherers into the cities, saying “These are a small band; they enrage us; and we are all on guard.”
Allah took the people of Fir'awn out of gardens, springs, treasures and a noble station, and gave it as an inheritance to the Children of Israel.
They pursued them at sunrise; when the two hosts saw each other, the companions of Musa said “We are about to be overtaken”; he said “No; my Lord is with me; He will guide me.”
Allah inspired Musa “Strike the sea with your staff”; it split, and each part was like a great mountain.

In Surah Ta-Ha, Allah told him to strike for them a dry path in the sea, fearing neither being overtaken nor any other danger; Fir'awn followed them with his soldiers and the sea covered them with what covered them.
Allah brought the others near, saved Musa and all who were with him, and then drowned the others; in that is a sign, and most of them were not believers.
Allah says that He parted the sea for them and saved them and drowned the family of Fir'awn while they were watching.

Allah says that He took the Children of Israel across the sea, and Fir'awn and his soldiers followed in transgression and enmity; when drowning overtook him he said “I believe that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims.”

He was told “Now? While you disobeyed before and were among the corrupters? Today We will save you in your body, so that you may be a sign for those who come after you; many people are heedless of Our signs.”

Surah Ad-Dukhan says that Musa was told to leave the sea calm, for they were a host to be drowned; and that Allah saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating punishment, from Fir'awn, who was high and among the transgressors.

Fir'awn and his soldiers were arrogant in the land without right and thought they would not be returned to Allah; Allah seized him and his soldiers and cast them into the sea, made them leaders calling to the Fire, followed them with a curse in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the despised.
Fir'awn wished to drive them from the land, and Allah drowned him and those with him all together.

chapters.summary_md: Musa was told to travel by night with Allah's servants and that they would be pursued [c1]. Fir'awn sent gatherers [c2]. At the sea, Musa said his Lord was with him [c4] and was told to strike it; it split [c5][c6]. Musa and those with him were saved and Fir'awn's host was drowned [c7][c8][c9].
chapters.body_md:
Allah inspired Musa to travel by night with His servants and told him they would be pursued [c1]. Fir'awn sent gatherers into the cities, calling Musa's people a small band who enraged him [c2]. Allah says He took the people of Fir'awn out of gardens, springs, treasures and a noble station and gave it as an inheritance to the Children of Israel [c3].

They pursued at sunrise; when the two hosts saw each other, Musa's companions said they were about to be overtaken, and Musa said his Lord was with him and would guide him [c4]. Allah told him to strike the sea with his staff, and it split, each part like a great mountain [c5]. Surah Ta-Ha says to strike a dry path in the sea, with no fear of being overtaken, and that the sea covered Fir'awn and his soldiers [c6]. Allah brought the others near, saved Musa and all with him, and drowned the others [c7]. Surah Al-Baqarah says Allah parted the sea and drowned the family of Fir'awn while the Children of Israel were watching [c8].

When drowning overtook Fir'awn, he said he believed that there is no god but the One in whom the Children of Israel believe; he was answered with “Now?” and told he would be saved in his body as a sign for those after him [c9][c10]. Surah Ad-Dukhan adds the order to leave the sea calm [c11]. Al-Qasas says Allah cast Fir'awn and his soldiers into the sea [c12]. Surah Al-Isra says Fir'awn wished to drive them from the land and Allah drowned him and those with him together [c13].
chapters.deep_md: Seven surahs touch the crossing. Ash-Shu'ara gives the fullest sequence: the command, the pursuit, the fear, the sea, the rescue and the drowning [c1][c4][c5][c7]. Ta-Ha says ‘a dry path’ [c6]; Ad-Dukhan says to leave the sea calm [c11]. The words ‘in your body’ in 10:92 [c10] are stated in the text without explanation. The exchange with the drowning Fir'awn [c9][c10] appears only in Yunus. In the surahs that name the inheritance of gardens and springs [c3] the ayat do not say that it was the same land as the one spoken of in other chapters of this account.
chapters.kids_md: Allah told Musa to leave at night with his people. Fir'awn's army followed them. When Musa's people saw the army and the sea, they were afraid, but Musa said his Lord was with him [c1][c4]. Allah told Musa to strike the sea with his staff, and it opened a path. Musa and his people were saved [c5][c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: the group's fear at the sea is answered by one sentence, “my Lord is with me; He will guide me” [c4]. The passage may be read as a reminder of reliance on Allah when there seems to be no way out.
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in the ayat: the name or the place of the sea (the ayat say bahr and yamm); the date; the number of people who crossed; the place on the far shore; and what Allah did with the body of Fir'awn beyond saving it ‘in your body’ as a sign (Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: any identification of a body with a named king). The “land” inherited in 26:59 and 44:28 is not named. The word rahwan in 44:24 (rendered “calm”) is understood in more than one way by interpreters.

claims.statement_en: Allah says He shaded them with the cloud and sent down upon them al-mann and as-salwa (rendered here manna and salwa), telling them to eat of the good things He provided; they did not wrong Him, but they wronged themselves.

When Musa asked for water for his people, Allah told him to strike the stone with his staff, and twelve springs gushed from it; each people knew its drinking place; they were told to eat and drink of Allah's provision and not to spread corruption in the land.
Allah divided them into twelve tribes, as nations.

They said “Musa, we cannot endure one kind of food, so call upon your Lord to bring forth for us of what the earth grows, its herbs, cucumbers, fum, lentils and onions” (fum is rendered by interpreters as garlic or as wheat); he said “Would you exchange what is better for what is lower? Go down to a town (misran), for you will have what you asked.”

They were told to enter a town, eat from it wherever they wished, enter the gate prostrating, and say “Hittah” so that Allah would forgive their mistakes; those who did wrong changed the word that was said to them, and Allah sent a punishment (rijz) from the heaven on them.

In Surah Ta-Ha, Allah recalls to the Children of Israel that He saved them from their enemy, promised them the right side of the mountain, and sent down the manna and the salwa; He warns them not to transgress in it, for His anger would descend; and says He is Forgiving to the one who repents, believes and does good and then is guided.

Musa reminded his people of Allah's favour, that He placed prophets among them, made them kings and gave them what He had not given anyone in the worlds, and told them to enter the holy land which Allah had assigned to them and not to turn back.

They said “Musa, there is a people of tyrants in it, and we will not enter until they leave; if they leave, we will enter”; two men of those who feared, whom Allah had favoured, said “Enter upon them by the gate; when you enter it, you will be the victors; and rely upon Allah, if you are believers.”
They said “Musa, we will never enter it as long as they are in it; so go, you and your Lord, and fight; we are sitting here.”

Musa said “My Lord, I have power over none but myself and my brother, so separate us from the defiantly disobedient people.” Allah said the land would be forbidden to them for forty years, during which they would wander in the earth, and told Musa not to grieve over the defiantly disobedient people.

chapters.summary_md: In the wilderness the Children of Israel were shaded and given manna and salwa [c1] and water from a stone [c2]. They asked for other foods [c4]. When told to enter the holy land they refused [c8][c9], and Musa asked to be separated from them; Allah said the land would be forbidden for forty years [c10].
chapters.body_md:
Allah says He shaded them with the cloud and sent down the manna and the salwa, telling them to eat of the good things [c1]. When Musa asked for water for his people, he was told to strike the stone with his staff, and twelve springs gushed forth, each people knowing its drinking place [c2]; they were divided into twelve tribes [c3]. They then said they could not endure one kind of food, and asked for herbs, cucumbers, fum, lentils and onions; Musa asked if they would exchange better for lower [c4]. They were told to enter a town, eat freely, enter the gate prostrating and say “Hittah”; those who did wrong changed the word and a punishment was sent from the heaven [c5]. Surah Ta-Ha recalls the favours and warns against transgression, while saying that Allah forgives the one who repents [c6].

Surah Al-Ma'idah records Musa's reminder of the favours, and the command to enter the holy land [c7]. His people said there were tyrants and that they would not enter until they left; two men whom Allah had favoured said to enter by the gate and rely on Allah [c8]. His people answered that they would never enter and that Musa and his Lord should go and fight while they sat [c9]. Musa said he had power only over himself and his brother and asked to be separated from them; Allah said the land was forbidden to them for forty years while they wandered [c10].
chapters.deep_md: Provision (manna, salwa, shade, water) [c1][c2] and refusal (the foods [c4], the gate [c5], the land [c8][c9]) are interwoven in these surahs without a fixed order. The word misran in [c4] can be read as ‘a town’ or as the name Misr; the text is left untranslated in meaning and flagged for review. In Al-Ma'idah the forty-year ruling [c10] follows Musa's own words that he has power only over himself and his brother. The ‘town’ of [c5] and the ‘holy land’ of [c7] are not stated to be the same place.
chapters.kids_md: In the desert Allah gave Musa's people shade, food and water. Allah told Musa to strike a stone, and springs came out of it [c1][c2]. Later Musa told his people to enter the holy land, but they were afraid and said they would sit where they were [c7][c9].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: the account sets Allah's provision [c1][c2] beside the people's complaints [c4] and refusals [c9]. Two men who feared still urged trust in Allah [c8].
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in the ayat: the place of the wandering, the identity of the “two men” in 5:23 (Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text; none is used here), the names of the tribes, the identity of the “town” and the “holy land” (the ayat do not name them), how the “punishment from the heaven” of 2:59 took place, and whether the forty years began at once. Hadith to add later: reports on the manna and the salwa and on the two men.

chapters.title_en: The appointed time and the tablets

claims.statement_en: Allah appointed thirty nights for Musa and completed them with ten, so that the appointed time of his Lord was forty nights; Musa said to his brother Harun “Take my place among my people, set things right, and do not follow the way of the corrupters.”
In Surah Ta-Ha, Allah asked “What made you hasten from your people, Musa?” and he said “They are on my track, and I hastened to You, my Lord, so that You would be pleased.”

When Musa came at the appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he said “My Lord, show me, that I may look at You.” Allah said “You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it stays in its place, then you will see Me.”
When his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble, and Musa fell unconscious; when he recovered he said “Glory be to You; I repent to You, and I am the first of the believers.”
Allah said “Musa, I have chosen you over the people with My messages and My speech; so take what I have given you and be among the grateful.”
Allah wrote for him in the tablets (al-alwah) of everything, an admonition and a detailing of everything, and told him to take them with strength and command his people to take the best of them.

Allah says He will turn away from His signs those who are arrogant in the land without right, so that even if they see every sign they do not believe, and that those who denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, their deeds are worthless.
Allah says that He gave Musa the Book and the Criterion (al-furqan) so that they might be guided.
When Musa's anger subsided he took up the tablets, and in what was written in them was guidance and mercy for those who fear their Lord.

Musa chose seventy men of his people for Allah's appointment; when the quake seized them he said “My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before, and me. Would You destroy us for what the foolish among us did? It is only Your trial, by which You lead astray whom You will and guide whom You will; You are our protector, so forgive us and have mercy on us.”

Musa asked for good in this world and the Hereafter, saying “we have turned to You”; Allah said His punishment strikes whom He wills, and His mercy encompasses all things, and He will prescribe it for those who are mindful, give zakat and believe in His signs.

chapters.summary_md: Allah appointed a time of forty nights for Musa, and he left Harun in charge of his people [c1]. Musa asked to look at his Lord, and the mountain crumbled [c3][c4]. Allah told him He had chosen him with His messages and speech [c5], and wrote the tablets for him [c6]. Musa also chose seventy men for the appointment [c10].
chapters.body_md:
Allah appointed thirty nights for Musa and completed them with ten, so that the appointed time was forty nights; Musa told Harun to take his place and set things right [c1]. In Ta-Ha Allah asked what made him hasten from his people, and he said he hastened so that Allah would be pleased [c2]. When he came at the appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he asked to look at Allah; Allah said he would not see Him, but to look at the mountain [c3]. When Allah manifested to the mountain it crumbled and Musa fell unconscious; when he recovered he said “Glory be to You; I repent to You, and I am the first of the believers” [c4]. Allah said He had chosen him over the people with His messages and speech and told him to take what He gave and be grateful [c5]. He wrote for Musa in the tablets of everything, an admonition and a detailing, and told him to take them with strength and command his people to take the best of them [c6]. Surah Al-Baqarah says Allah gave Musa the Book and the Criterion [c8]. Allah also says He will turn the arrogant away from His signs [c7].

After his anger subsided he took up the tablets; in their writing was guidance and mercy [c9]. Musa chose seventy men for the appointment, and when the quake seized them he prayed for forgiveness and mercy [c10]. Allah answered that His mercy encompassed all things and would be prescribed for those who are mindful [c11].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat give Musa's meeting with his Lord as an appointed time with a stated length [c1], a request [c3], an event on the mountain [c4], and a reply that names three things Allah gave: the messages, the speech and the tablets [c5][c6]. The word furqan in Al-Baqarah [c8] is rendered here ‘Criterion’ and is a topic for scholarly review. The ayat 7:154-156 appear after the story of the calf in the surah, but the text gives no statement that the seventy men were chosen after it; this draft does not claim an order. Whether the “quake” of 7:155 and the “thunderbolt” of 2:55 are the same event is a question for scholars and not decided here.
chapters.kids_md: Allah called Musa to meet Him for forty nights. Musa left his brother Harun to look after the people [c1]. Allah spoke to Musa and gave him tablets with guidance written in them [c5][c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: Musa asks for something and is told what he cannot have, with a sign given instead [c3][c4]. He then responds with repentance and the first words of faith [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in the ayat: what the tablets looked like or were made of, what was written in them beyond the general description, where the appointment was, who the seventy men were, and whether the thirty and ten nights were separate stages. The nature of the manifestation (7:143) is stated only as Allah manifested Himself to the mountain; this draft gives no further description. Hadith to add later: reports on the tablets and on the seventy.

claims.statement_en: After Allah took the Children of Israel across the sea, they came upon a people devoted to idols of theirs and said “Musa, make for us a god as they have gods”; he said “You are a people who are ignorant”, and “Shall I seek for you any god other than Allah, when He has favoured you over the worlds?”
Allah told Musa “We have tried your people after you, and the Samiri has led them astray.”

Musa returned to his people angry and grieved and said “My people, did your Lord not promise you a good promise? Did the covenant seem long to you, or did you want anger from your Lord to descend on you, so you broke your promise to me?”

They said “We did not break our promise to you of our own will, but we were made to carry loads of the people's ornaments, so we threw them, and so did the Samiri cast”; he brought out for them a calf, a body that had a lowing, and they said “This is your god and the god of Musa.” (The next word, fa-nasiya, has its subject read differently by interpreters and is not translated here.)

Allah says that they did not see that it returned no word to them and had no power to harm or benefit them; and that people of Musa took, after he left, a calf from their ornaments, a body having a lowing, and it neither spoke to them nor guided them to a way.

Harun had said to them before “My people, you are only being tried with it; your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my order”; they said “We will not cease to be devoted to it until Musa returns to us.”

Musa said to Harun “What prevented you, when you saw them go astray, from following me? Did you disobey my order?” Harun said “Son of my mother, do not seize my beard or my head; I feared that you would say, ‘You caused division among the Children of Israel and did not observe my word.’”

In Surah Al-A'raf, Musa returned angry and grieved, said “What an evil thing you did in my place after me! Did you hasten the command of your Lord?”, threw down the tablets and seized his brother's head, pulling him toward him; Harun said “Son of my mother, the people deemed me weak and nearly killed me, so do not let the enemies rejoice at me and do not put me with the wrongdoing people.”
Musa said “My Lord, forgive me and my brother and admit us into Your mercy; You are the most merciful of the merciful.”

Musa asked the Samiri “What is your case, Samiri?” He said “I saw what they did not see, so I took a handful from the track of the messenger and threw it, and thus my soul suggested to me.” Musa said “Go; in this life it is for you to say ‘No touching’; and you have an appointment you will not miss; look at your god to which you were devoted; we will burn it and scatter it in the sea.”
Musa said “Your God is only Allah, other than whom there is no god; He has encompassed all things in knowledge.”
When they regretted and saw that they had gone astray, they said “If our Lord does not have mercy on us and forgive us, we will surely be among the losers.”

Allah says those who took the calf will be struck by anger from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world, while your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful to those who did evil, then repented and believed.
In Surah Al-Baqarah, Allah says that He appointed forty nights for Musa and then they took the calf after he left, being wrongdoers; then He pardoned them after that so that they might be thankful.

Musa said to his people “My people, you have wronged yourselves by taking the calf, so repent to your Maker and kill yourselves (fa-qtulu anfusakum); that is better for you with your Maker”; and He accepted their repentance.

chapters.summary_md: After the crossing the Children of Israel asked Musa for a god like those of a people devoted to idols [c1]. While Musa was away, the Samiri brought out a calf, and they took it [c2][c4][c5]. Musa returned angry [c3][c8], questioned Harun [c7][c8], and the Samiri [c10]. The people repented [c12]; Allah says He pardoned them [c14].
chapters.body_md:
After the crossing the people came upon others devoted to idols and asked Musa to make them a god; he said they were ignorant and asked whether he should seek a god other than Allah [c1]. While Musa was away, Allah told him that his people had been tried and that the Samiri had led them astray [c2]. Musa returned angry and grieved and asked whether the covenant had seemed long to them [c3]. They said they were made to carry loads of the people's ornaments, threw them, and that the Samiri cast too; he brought out a calf, a body with a lowing, and they said “This is your god and the god of Musa” [c4]. Allah says it returned no word and had no power to harm or benefit [c5]. Harun had said they were being tried by it and to follow him; they said they would keep to it until Musa returned [c6].

Musa asked Harun what had prevented him, and Harun answered about seizing his beard or head and his fear of division [c7]. Al-A'raf records Musa throwing down the tablets and seizing his brother's head, and Harun's answer that the people deemed him weak and nearly killed him [c8]. Musa prayed for forgiveness for himself and his brother [c9]. He asked the Samiri what his case was; the Samiri said he took a handful from the track of the messenger and threw it, as his soul suggested [c10]. Musa told him that his god would be burned and scattered in the sea [c10], and said that their God is only Allah [c11].

The people, when they regretted, asked for mercy and forgiveness [c12]. Allah says those who took the calf would be struck by anger and humiliation, and that He is Forgiving to those who repent [c13]. Al-Baqarah says Allah pardoned them after the forty nights [c14], and records Musa telling them to repent to their Maker and kill themselves, and that He accepted their repentance [c15].
chapters.deep_md: Three surahs give three accounts of the calf. Ta-Ha has the longest sequence: Allah's information to Musa [c2], the people's explanation [c4], Harun's earlier warning [c6], Musa's exchange with Harun [c7] and the Samiri [c10]. Al-A'raf has the shorter account of the calf [c5], with Musa's reaction in physical terms and Harun's answer in different words [c8]; Harun's answer here is that the people deemed him weak. The two answers, [c7] and [c8], are both stated in the text and are not set against one another in this draft. Al-Baqarah places the calf after the forty nights [c14] and records the instruction to ‘kill yourselves’ [c15]; the meaning of this command is a matter for interpreters.
chapters.kids_md: While Musa was away, the Samiri made a calf, and many of the people began to follow it. Harun told them it was a test and that their Lord is the Most Merciful [c4][c6]. When Musa came back he was upset. He said that their God is only Allah [c11]. The people were sorry and asked Allah for mercy [c12].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: the account shows a community being led away in a leader's absence [c4], a brother who warned them [c6], and the opening of repentance afterwards [c12][c14]. It is for reflection, not a rule drawn from the ayat.
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in the ayat: what the calf was made of beyond ‘a body having a lowing’ (the ayat say it was made of the people's ornaments), the Samiri's origin, what ‘a handful from the track of the messenger’ refers to (interpreters differ; Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: any identification of the ‘messenger’ and the ‘track’), how the repentance of 2:54 was carried out, and the number of those who took the calf. Hadith to add later: reports on the Samiri's handful.

claims.statement_en: Allah says He took their covenant and raised the mountain (at-Tur) above them, saying “Take what We have given you with strength and remember what is in it, so that you may be mindful.”

In Surah Al-A'raf, Allah says He lifted the mountain above them as if it were a canopy and they thought it was going to fall on them, and told them to take what He gave them with strength and remember what is in it.

In Surah Al-Baqarah, after reminding them of the covenant and the mountain, Allah says they said “We hear and we disobey”, and that the calf was made to sink into their hearts because of their disbelief.
In Surah An-Nisa, Allah says He raised the mountain above them with their covenant, told them to enter the gate prostrating and not to transgress on the Sabbath, and took from them a solemn covenant.

chapters.summary_md: Four ayat in three surahs recall a covenant taken from the Children of Israel with the mountain raised above them [c1][c2][c4]. They were told to take what they had been given with strength and to remember what is in it [c1][c2]. One recalls that they said “We hear and we disobey” [c3].
chapters.body_md: Allah says He took the covenant of the Children of Israel and raised the mountain above them, telling them to take what He had given them with strength and to remember what is in it [c1]. Al-A'raf describes the mountain lifted above them as if a canopy, so that they thought it would fall on them [c2]. Al-Baqarah 2:93 repeats the reminder, adds that they said “We hear and we disobey”, and that the calf was made to sink into their hearts because of disbelief [c3]. An-Nisa mentions the raising of the mountain with their covenant, the command to enter the gate prostrating, and not to transgress on the Sabbath, and a solemn covenant [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The four ayat do not say where the covenant fits in the order of the other events in this account. Three of them speak of ‘taking what We gave you with strength’ [c1][c2]. Al-Baqarah 2:93 ties the covenant to their reply and to the calf [c3]. An-Nisa 4:154 lists the content of the covenant as gate, prostration and Sabbath [c4]; the ‘gate’ is spoken of in the chapter on provision and the wilderness [see that chapter], where the ayat do not say that it is the same gate.
chapters.kids_md: Allah took a promise from the Children of Israel and told them to hold on to what He gave them with strength and remember what is in it [c1][c2]. They said, “We hear and we disobey” [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: hearing a command is different from obeying it, and the ayat set the two side by side in the people's own words [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in the ayat: when this took place in relation to the tablets or the calf, the nature of the raising of the mountain (interpreters differ on whether it is literal), and what the ‘gate’ and the Sabbath refer to in 4:154. The relation between 2:63 and 2:93 (a repeated reminder in the same surah) is a matter for scholars.
