claims.statement_en: Musa said to his young man “I will not cease until I reach the meeting of the two seas, or I will go on for a long time.”

When they reached the meeting of the two, they forgot their fish, and it took its way into the sea; after they passed on, Musa asked for their meal, saying they had met with fatigue on the journey; the young man said he had forgotten the fish at the rock and only Shaytan made him forget to mention it; Musa said “That is what we were seeking”, and they went back retracing their steps.
They found a servant from among Allah's servants, to whom He had given mercy from Himself and taught knowledge from Himself.

Musa asked “May I follow you on condition that you teach me of what you have been taught of right guidance?” He said “You will never be able to be patient with me; and how can you be patient about what you have not encompassed in knowledge?”
Musa said “You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any order”; he said “If you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I myself mention it to you.”

When they boarded the boat he made a hole in it; Musa said “Did you make a hole in it to drown its people? You have done a grave thing.” He said “Did I not say that you would never be able to be patient with me?” Musa said “Do not hold me to account for what I forgot, and do not burden me with difficulty in my affair.”

They met a boy and he killed him; Musa said “Have you killed a pure soul, not for a soul? You have done a terrible thing.” He repeated his earlier question, and Musa said “If I ask you about anything after this, do not keep me as a companion; you have received an excuse from me.”

They came to the people of a town and asked for food, and the people refused to host them; they found in it a wall about to fall, and he set it straight; Musa said “If you wished, you could have taken a payment for it.”
He said “This is the parting between me and you; I will inform you of the interpretation of what you were not able to be patient about.”
The boat belonged to poor people working at sea; he wished to damage it because behind them was a king seizing every boat by force.

The servant said the boy's parents were believers and “we feared” that he would burden them with transgression and disbelief, so “we wished” that their Lord would give them in exchange one better than him in purity and nearer in mercy.

The wall belonged to two orphan boys in the town, and beneath it was a treasure for them; their father was righteous, and your Lord wished that they reach their maturity and take out their treasure as a mercy from your Lord; “I did not do it of my own accord. That is the interpretation of what you were not able to be patient about.”

chapters.summary_md: Musa set out with his young man to the meeting of the two seas [c1] and lost their fish [c2]. They found a servant given mercy and knowledge [c3]. Musa asked to follow him and was warned he would not be able to be patient [c4]. Three events puzzled Musa [c6][c7][c8]; the servant then gave the interpretation of each [c10][c11][c12].
chapters.body_md:
Musa told his young man he would not cease until reaching the meeting of the two seas [c1]. They forgot the fish there, and it went into the sea; when they stopped for their meal, the young man said he had forgotten it, and Musa said that was what they were seeking, and they went back [c2]. They found a servant from among Allah's servants, given mercy and knowledge from Allah [c3]. Musa asked to follow him to be taught, and the servant said he would not be able to be patient with what he had not encompassed in knowledge [c4]. Musa said he would be patient and obedient; the servant told him not to ask about anything until he himself mentioned it [c5].

Then three events occur. He made a hole in a boat; Musa objected and was reminded of the condition [c6]. He killed a boy; Musa objected again and said that if he asked again the servant should not keep him as a companion [c7]. In a town that had refused them hospitality, he set a wall straight, and Musa said he could have taken payment [c8]. He said it was the parting and he would give the interpretation [c9].

The boat belonged to poor people, and a king seized every boat by force [c10]. The servant said the boy's parents were believers and “we feared” he would burden them with transgression and disbelief, so “we wished” for one better in exchange [c11]. The wall belonged to two orphans with a treasure beneath it, from a righteous father; their Lord wished them to reach maturity and take out the treasure, and the servant said he had not done it on his own accord [c12].
chapters.deep_md: The passage has a framing of travel and a loss [c1][c2], a request and a condition [c4][c5], three incidents each answered by Musa's objection [c6][c7][c8], and three explanations [c10][c11][c12]. In the explanations the speaker moves between ‘I wished’ [c10], ‘we feared … we wished’ [c11] and ‘your Lord wished’ [c12], while ending with ‘I did not do it of my own accord’ [c12]. The ayat state the interpretation of each act and do not state anything further about the servant's knowledge. The passage is where Musa is shown as a learner.
chapters.kids_md: Musa travelled to find a servant of Allah who had special knowledge. He asked to follow him and learn. The servant said Musa would not be able to be patient [c3][c4]. Then three things happened that Musa did not understand [c6][c7][c8], and at the end the servant explained each one [c10][c11][c12].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: the account is about the limits of what a person sees at one moment [c4], and it records that each act had a reason that could only be told afterwards [c10][c11][c12]. It also shows a prophet asking to learn from another [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md: Not established in the ayat: the name of the servant (Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name al-Khidr, which appears in hadith literature; hadith to add later), the name of Musa's young man (Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text), the place called the meeting of the two seas, the identity of the king, the town, the boy and the orphans, and the kind of fish. The ayat say 'Musa' and do not add 'son of Imran'; the inventory reads this as the same Musa as the rest of this story, which is the common reading. Whether the servant was a prophet is not stated (the ayat say he was given mercy and knowledge from Allah). The ages of the boy and the orphans are not given.

claims.statement_en: Allah says He sent Musa with His signs: “Bring your people out from the darknesses to the light, and remind them of the days of Allah.”

Musa said to his people “Remember Allah's favour upon you when He saved you from the family of Fir'awn, who inflicted on you the worst of torment, slaughtering your sons and keeping your women alive; in that was a great trial from your Lord.”

Allah announced “If you are grateful, I will surely increase you; but if you are ungrateful, My punishment is severe”; and Musa said “If you are ungrateful, you and all those on earth, Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy.”
Musa said to his people “My people, why do you harm me when you know that I am the messenger of Allah to you?” and when they deviated, Allah let their hearts deviate.

Allah says He bestowed favour on Musa and Harun, saved them and their people from the great distress, helped them so that they were the victors, gave them the clear Book, guided them to the straight path, left a good mention of them among later generations, and said “Peace be upon Musa and Harun”; they were among His believing servants.

Allah says He gave Musa nine clear signs; Musa was told to ask the Children of Israel when he came to them; Fir'awn said “I think you, Musa, are bewitched”, and Musa said “You know that none sent these down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as clear proofs, and I think, Fir'awn, that you are doomed.”

Fir'awn wished to drive them out of the land and Allah drowned him and those with him together; after him Allah said to the Children of Israel “Dwell in the land, and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you all together.”

chapters.summary_md: Musa was sent to bring his people from the darknesses to the light and to remind them of Allah's days [c1][c2]. The ayat record his words on gratitude [c3] and on being harmed by his own people [c4], and Allah's praise and peace upon Musa and Harun [c5]. They also recall the nine signs and the end of Fir'awn [c6][c7].
chapters.body_md:
Allah says He sent Musa with His signs to bring his people out from the darknesses to the light and remind them of the days of Allah [c1]. Musa told them to remember Allah's favour in saving them from the family of Fir'awn [c2]. Allah announced that gratitude brings increase and ingratitude a severe punishment, and Musa said that if all on earth were ungrateful, Allah is Free of need [c3]. Musa also asked his people why they harmed him when they knew he was the messenger of Allah to them; when they deviated, Allah let their hearts deviate [c4].

Surah As-Saffat says Allah bestowed favour on Musa and Harun, saved them and their people, helped them, gave them the clear Book and the straight path, left a good mention of them and said “Peace be upon Musa and Harun” [c5]. Surah Al-Isra says Allah gave Musa nine clear signs, and records Fir'awn calling him bewitched and Musa calling Fir'awn doomed [c6]. It adds that Fir'awn wished to drive them out of the land and was drowned, and the Children of Israel were told to dwell in the land [c7].
chapters.deep_md: This closing chapter gathers statements about Musa that stand outside a single scene. The speech of Musa to his people is given as a reminder of favour and a statement on gratitude [c2][c3]. The ayat of Ibrahim 14:5-8 and As-Saffat 37:114-122 present the same messenger from two sides: what he told his people [c1][c2][c3] and what Allah says of him and Harun [c5]. Al-Isra' 17:101 states “nine clear signs” [c6]; the nine are not listed in the same ayah.
chapters.kids_md: Allah sent Musa to teach his people to remember Allah and to be thankful [c1][c3]. Allah says that He gave Musa and Harun the Book and guided them [c5]. Allah says “Peace be upon Musa and Harun” [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation, not scripture: the ayat state a principle in Musa's words, that gratitude brings increase [c3], and they record that a prophet can be harmed by his own people while his message stands [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md: What the Quranic text does not state about Musa, as far as the ayat in this draft go: his death, burial or age; the name of his wife and children; the fate of Harun beyond the ayat cited; the dates of any event; the number of the Children of Israel; the name or period of Fir'awn; the list of the nine signs; the fate of the believing magicians; the cow of Banu Isra'il (2:67-73, not covered in this draft). The Torah and the later traditions of the Children of Israel are outside this phase. Hadith to add later: reports on the life and death of Musa and on his meeting with other prophets.

uncertainties_en: The identity and name of Fir'awn are not given in the Quran; none is used here.

Names found only in later tradition (the mother, sister and wife of Musa; the father of the two women of Madyan; the servant; Musa's young man; the two men of 5:23; the believing man of Fir'awn's family) are not in the chapters.
Surah order is not chronology. The Quran tells the call, the signs, the magicians and the sea in several surahs; the chapters keep them separate and do not merge them.
The speaker of 28:19 is not marked in the text; interpreters differ.

The meaning of 'fa-qtulu anfusakum' (2:54), 'qiblah' (10:87), 'misran' (2:61), the 'greatest sign' (79:20), the 'quake' (7:155) and the 'thunderbolt' (2:55) is read in more than one way; the draft translations are for review.
Whether the Musa of 18:60-82 is the Musa of the other ayat is the common reading but is not stated in the ayat as 'son of Imran'.
The cow of Banu Isra'il (2:67-73) and the Qarun account (28:76-82) are not covered in this draft.
Hadith to add later: reports on the staff, the Samiri, the plagues, the servant, the death of Musa, and the meetings of prophets.
